Fix a spatial dimension $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, side length $L>0$, and odd integer $N\ge3$. Put $h=L/N$ and $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$. The periodic grid has index set $J_N=(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^d$ and nodes $x_j=hj$ modulo $L$. A grid scalar is a real array $u=(u_j)_{j\in J_N}$; a grid vector has $d$ real components at each node. Define
$$ \langle u,v\rangle_h=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}u_jv_j,\qquad \|u\|_h=\langle u,u\rangle_h^{1/2},\qquad \bar u=L^{-d}h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}u_j . $$ The same pairing is componentwise for grid vectors. For the coordinate vector $e_a$, define the centered field difference and positive periodic Poisson stencil by $$ (D_a^0u)_j=\frac{u_{j+e_a}-u_{j-e_a}}{2h},\qquad (A_hu)_j=\sum_{a=1}^d\frac{2u_j-u_{j+e_a}-u_{j-e_a}}{h^2}. $$
All indices wrap modulo $N$. The discrete Fourier index set is $\mathcal K_N=\{-\frac{N-1}{2},\ldots,\frac{N-1}{2}\}^d$; the character at $k\in\mathcal K_N$ is $j\mapsto e^{2\pi i k\cdot j/N}$. This odd-grid convention has no Nyquist mode.

derivations.claim: In one coordinate, on a cell $[a,a+h]$, put $K(x)=(x-a)(a+h-x)/2$. Two integrations by parts give $\frac h2(f(a)+f(a+h))-\int_a^{a+h}f(x)\,dx=\int_a^{a+h}K(x)f''(x)\,dx .$ Since $K\ge0$ and $\int_a^{a+h}K(x)\,dx=h^3/12$, the absolute cell error is at most $h^3\|f''\|_\infty/12$. Sum over the $N$ periodic cells, whose endpoint contributions assemble into the periodic trapezoid sum $h\sum_j f(jh)$. This gives the one-dimensional error bound $Lh^2\|f''\|_\infty/12$.

For each coordinate $a$, let $Q_a$ denote the periodic trapezoid operator in that coordinate and $I_a$ integration over that coordinate. Both have sup-norm operator bound at most $L$, since their weights are nonnegative and sum to $L$. The telescoping identity $Q_1\cdots Q_d-I_1\cdots I_d =\sum_{a=1}^d Q_1\cdots Q_{a-1}(Q_a-I_a)I_{a+1}\cdots I_d$ holds by cancellation. In the $a$th summand, the one-dimensional bound from step 1.1 applies after the later-coordinate integrations; differentiation in coordinate $a$ commutes with those integrations. The other $d-1$ operators contribute at most $L^{d-1}$ in sup norm. Thus that summand is bounded by $L^dh^2\|\partial_{aa}f\|_\infty/12$. Summing these bounds gives the displayed estimate, because $Q_1\cdots Q_d f=h^d\sum_jf(x_j)$ and $I_1\cdots I_df=\int_{[0,L]^d}f$.

derivations.claim: Reindex the finite periodic sums in each coordinate. For any real arrays $u,v$, $\langle u,A_hv\rangle_h =h^d\sum_{a=1}^d\sum_j \frac{(u_{j+e_a}-u_j)(v_{j+e_a}-v_j)}{h^2}.$ The right side is symmetric in $u,v$ and is nonnegative when $u=v$. Thus $A_h$ is self-adjoint and nonnegative.

If $\langle u,A_hu\rangle_h=0$, every nonnegative squared difference in step 1.1 is zero, so $u_{j+e_a}=u_j$ for every $j,a$. Coordinate steps connect every pair of indices in $J_N$, hence $u$ is constant. Conversely a constant is annihilated by $A_h$.

For a symmetric finite-dimensional linear map, $\operatorname{ran}A_h=(\ker A_h)^\perp$: symmetry gives $\operatorname{ran}A_h\subseteq(\ker A_h)^\perp$, and rank-nullity makes the dimensions equal. By step 2.1, $(\ker A_h)^\perp$ is precisely the zero-mean subspace. Therefore each zero-mean $s$ is in the range, and any two solutions differ by a constant; imposing $\bar\phi=0$ selects exactly one.

For $e_k(j)=e^{2\pi i k\cdot j/N}$, substitution in the stencil from [F1] gives $(A_he_k)_j =\frac1{h^2}\sum_a\left(2-e^{2\pi i k_a/N}-e^{-2\pi i k_a/N}\right)e_k(j) =\lambda_h(k)e_k(j).$ The characters form a basis because their finite geometric sums are orthogonal: in one coordinate $\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}e^{2\pi i(k-\ell)j/N}$ is $N$ if $k=\ell$ modulo $N$ and $0$ otherwise; taking products gives $N^d$ independent characters. $$\gamma_{N,L}= \max_{\substack{k\in\mathcal K_N\\k\ne0}} \frac{\left(\sum_{a=1}^d h^{-2}\sin^2(2\pi k_a/N)\right)^{1/2}} {4h^{-2}\sum_{a=1}^d\sin^2(\pi k_a/N)} .$$ For the centered field operator $D^0=(D_a^0)_{a=1}^d$, $$\|D^0(\phi-\widetilde\phi)\|_h\le\gamma_{N,L}\|r\|_h,\qquad \gamma_{N,L}\le\frac{h}{2\sin(\pi/N)}\le\frac L4 .$$ For any particle location $x_p$ and charge-to-mass ratio $q_p/m_p$ with $m_p>0$, the force gather using the weights of [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]] obeys $$\left|\frac{q_p}{m_p}G_{x_p}\!\left(-D^0\phi+D^0\widetilde\phi\right)\right| \le\frac{|q_p|}{m_p}h^{-d/2}\gamma_{N,L}\|r\|_h .$$
Thus the norm in the force certificate is the actual finite-grid inverse/derivative norm; the explicit $h^{-d/2}$ conversion is retained when passing from grid $L^2$ to a particle gather.

Fix a spatial dimension $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, side length $L>0$, and odd integer $N\ge3$. Put $h=L/N$ and $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$. The periodic grid has index set $J_N=(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^d$ and nodes $x_j=hj$ modulo $L$. A grid scalar is a real array $u=(u_j)_{j\in J_N}$; a grid vector has $d$ real components at each node. Define
$$ \langle u,v\rangle_h=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}u_jv_j,\qquad \|u\|_h=\langle u,u\rangle_h^{1/2},\qquad \bar u=L^{-d}h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}u_j . $$ The same pairing is componentwise for grid vectors. For the coordinate vector $e_a$, define the centered field difference and positive periodic Poisson stencil by $$ (D_a^0u)_j=\frac{u_{j+e_a}-u_{j-e_a}}{2h},\qquad (A_hu)_j=\sum_{a=1}^d\frac{2u_j-u_{j+e_a}-u_{j-e_a}}{h^2}. $$
All indices wrap modulo $N$. The discrete Fourier index set is $\mathcal K_N=\{-\frac{N-1}{2},\ldots,\frac{N-1}{2}\}^d$; the character at $k\in\mathcal K_N$ is $j\mapsto e^{2\pi i k\cdot j/N}$. This odd-grid convention has no Nyquist mode.

On the torus and grid of [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]], an algebraic assignment shape is any family of functions $w_j:\mathbb T_L^d\to[0,\infty)$ such that $\sum_{j\in J_N}w_j(x)=1$ for every $x$. For the smooth fixed-$\varepsilon$ branch used in the force-error and ODE results, fix $\varepsilon>0$, put $\alpha_\varepsilon=e^{-\varepsilon/L}$ and choose the explicit even periodic kernel
$$ \eta_\varepsilon(x)=L^{-d}\prod_{a=1}^d \frac{1-\alpha_\varepsilon^2}{1-2\alpha_\varepsilon\cos(2\pi x_a/L)+\alpha_\varepsilon^2}. $$ For this smooth branch and each $x\in\mathbb T_L^d$, set $$ Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}\eta_\varepsilon(x_j-x),\qquad w_j^{\varepsilon,h}(x)=\frac{h^d\eta_\varepsilon(x_j-x)}{Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)}. $$ Each factor in the kernel denominator is positive, so $Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)>0$ and the smooth-branch weights are well-defined. For any algebraic shape family above and finitely many particle positions $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_P)$ with charges $q_1,\ldots,q_P\in\mathbb R$, write $Q=\sum_{p=1}^Pq_p$ and define deposited charge density $$ \rho_j(X)=h^{-d}\sum_{p=1}^Pq_pw_j(X_p)-Q/L^d . $$
For any grid scalar $g$, its potential gather is $(G_Xg)_p=\sum_jw_j(X_p)g_j$. For any grid vector $E$, its field gather is defined componentwise by the same weights, $(G_XE)_p=\sum_jw_j(X_p)E_j$. On the smooth fixed-$\varepsilon$ branch, $w_j$ means the explicit family $w_j^{\varepsilon,h}$ above.

Let $L>0$, odd $N\ge3$, $h=L/N$, and $f\in C^2(\mathbb T_L^d)$ for $d\in\{1,2,3\}$. With the uniform tensor grid $x_j=hj$ and indices taken modulo $N$,
$$ \left|h^d\sum_{j\in(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^d}f(x_j)-\int_{[0,L]^d}f(x)\,dx\right| \le \frac{L^dh^2}{12}\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_{aa}f\|_\infty . $$

Let $\eta_\varepsilon$ be the explicit product kernel in [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]], with $\alpha_\varepsilon=e^{-\varepsilon/L}\in(0,1)$. Let $\mu$ be a finite signed Borel measure on $\mathbb T_L^d$ with mass $Q$ and total variation $\|\mu\|_{\rm TV}$. Put
$$ \widehat\mu(k)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}e^{-2\pi i k\cdot y/L}\,d\mu(y),\qquad \kappa_k=2\pi k/L . $$ Then $\eta_\varepsilon$ is strictly positive, even, smooth, and has integral one. The regularized neutralized source $$ \rho_\varepsilon^\mu(x)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}\eta_\varepsilon(x-y)\,d\mu(y)-Q/L^d $$ is $C^\infty$ with zero mean. Its unique zero-mean periodic solution of $-\Delta\phi_\varepsilon^\mu=\rho_\varepsilon^\mu$ is the absolutely and uniformly differentiable Fourier series $$ \phi_\varepsilon^\mu(x)=L^{-d}\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}} \frac{\left(\prod_{a=1}^d\alpha_\varepsilon^{|k_a|}\right)\widehat\mu(k)} {|\kappa_k|^2}e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}. $$
For every integer $r\ge0$, all spatial derivative series of order at most $r$ converge absolutely and uniformly; their bounds may depend on $r,\varepsilon,L,\|\mu\|_{\rm TV}$.

derivations.claim: Strict positivity of $\eta_\varepsilon$ implies $Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)>0$. Summing the weights in [F2] gives $\sum_jw_j^{\varepsilon,h}(x)=Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)/Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)=1$, and each weight is nonnegative. Since every summand in $Z$ is at least $h^d\min\eta_\varepsilon$, and $h^d|J_N|=L^d$, $Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)\ge Z_{\min}$.

For fixed $x$, put $f_x(y)=\eta_\varepsilon(y-x)g(y)$ and let $q_x=h^d\sum_jf_x(x_j)-\int f_x(y)\,dy\in\mathbb R^m$. For every Euclidean unit vector $v$, apply the scalar estimate [F3] to $v\cdot f_x$. Since $|v\cdot\partial_{aa}f_x|\le|\partial_{aa}f_x|_2$, this gives $|v\cdot q_x|\le C_{\eta,g}h^2$. If $q_x\ne0$, take $v=q_x/|q_x|_2$; if $q_x=0$ the bound is immediate. Thus $|q_x|_2\le C_{\eta,g}h^2$, with no dimension factor. The integral is $(\eta_\varepsilon*g)(x)$ because the kernel is even. Projecting that integral onto its unit direction in the same way, nonnegativity and the unit integral [F4] give $|(\eta_\varepsilon*g)(x)|_2\le\|g\|_\infty$. The defining supremum is over both $x$ and $y$: translation of the kernel alone does not translate $g$.

Apply [F3] to $y\mapsto\eta_\varepsilon(y-x)$; translation does not change its second-derivative suprema and its integral is $1$ by [F4]. Thus $|Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)-1|\le C_\eta h^2$. By [F2], $(P_h^\varepsilon\mu)_j=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}\frac{\eta_\varepsilon(x_j-x)}{Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)}\,d\mu(x) .$ Subtract $(\eta_\varepsilon*\mu)(x_j)$, factor $\eta_\varepsilon(x_j-x)$, and use $|Z^{-1}-1|=|Z-1|/Z\le C_\eta h^2/Z_{\min}$. Integrating against the total variation measure gives the first bound.

The gathered sum in the Statement is $h^d\sum_j f_x(x_j)/Z_{\varepsilon,h}(x)$ by [F2]. Subtract the integral, use the quadrature error from step 1.2 divided by $Z\ge Z_{\min}$, and bound the Euclidean norm of the normalization correction by $|Z^{-1}-1|\|g\|_\infty\le C_\eta h^2\|g\|_\infty/Z_{\min}$. This is the second bound.

Use the grid, inner product, and operator $A_h$ of [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]]. Then $A_h$ is self-adjoint and nonnegative, $\ker A_h$ consists exactly of constant arrays, and $\operatorname{ran}A_h=\{s:\bar s=0\}$. Consequently, for every compatible source $\bar s=0$, there is a unique solution $\phi$ of $A_h\phi=s$ with the gauge $\bar\phi=0$.

For $k\in\mathcal K_N$, the Fourier character $e_k(j)=e^{2\pi i k\cdot j/N}$ is an eigenvector with
$$ \lambda_h(k)=\frac4{h^2}\sum_{a=1}^d\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\pi k_a}{N}\right). $$
Only $k=0$ has eigenvalue zero.

Input an odd $N\ge3$ periodic grid as in [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]] and a real grid source $s$. If $\bar s\ne0$, return the status incompatible-source. Otherwise compute the finite discrete Fourier coefficients $\widehat s_k=N^{-d}\sum_js_je^{-2\pi i k\cdot j/N}$. Set $\widehat\phi_0=0$ and, for each $k\ne0$, set $\widehat\phi_k=\widehat s_k/\lambda_h(k)$ with $\lambda_h(k)$ from [[thm-periodic-centered-difference-poisson-zero-mode-and-gauge]]. Return the inverse finite Fourier transform $\phi_j=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_N}\widehat\phi_ke^{2\pi i k\cdot j/N}$ and status success. All arithmetic here is exact real or complex arithmetic; an implementation using floating-point FFTs requires a separate perturbation analysis.

derivations.claim: The source and grid contain finitely many real numbers, so computing its mean and finite Fourier transform terminates. If $\bar s\ne0$, then the constant Fourier coefficient of $s$ is nonzero while $A_h$ annihilates constants and has zero constant coefficient on every output, so $A_h\phi=s$ is impossible.

If $\bar s=0$, its zero Fourier coefficient is zero. By [F1], every other eigenvalue is positive, so all divisions in [F2] are defined. For real input, $\widehat s_{-k}=\overline{\widehat s_k}$ and $\lambda_h(-k)=\lambda_h(k)$; therefore the returned coefficients have the same conjugate symmetry, and pairing the $k$ and $-k$ terms in the inverse transform shows every $\phi_j$ is real. For every nonzero mode, the returned coefficient satisfies $\lambda_h(k)\widehat\phi_k=\widehat s_k$, and the zero mode satisfies $0=\widehat s_0$. Inverse Fourier transformation therefore gives $A_h\phi=s$ and $\widehat\phi_0=0$ gives $\bar\phi=0$.
The coefficient list is finite, hence inverse transformation terminates. Uniqueness of the returned gauged solution follows from [F1].

Fix $\varepsilon>0$, $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $L>0$, and a regularized one-species model with total charge $Q$ and total mass $M>0$. Let $c=Q/M$. For each position $y\in\mathbb T_L^d$, define the continuous unit-source field by taking the zero-mean solution $\phi_\varepsilon^y$ from [[thm-periodic-pic-continuum-regularized-poisson-kernel-is-smooth]] for $\mu=\delta_y$, and setting
$$ \mathcal E_\varepsilon(x,y)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}\eta_\varepsilon(z-x)(-\nabla\phi_\varepsilon^y(z))\,dz =\frac1{L^d}\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}} \frac{-i\kappa_k}{|\kappa_k|^2} \left(\prod_{a=1}^d\alpha_\varepsilon^{2|k_a|}\right)e^{i\kappa_k\cdot(x-y)} . $$ The series converges absolutely with all derivatives by geometric summability. For the grid branch, let $\phi_h^y$ be the mean-zero solution of $$ A_h\phi_h^y=h^{-d}w^{\varepsilon,h}(y)-L^{-d}\mathbf1 $$ whose compatibility follows from [[thm-periodic-pic-charge-conservation-and-neutralized-source]], and put $$ \mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h}(x,y)=\sum_{j\in J_N}w_j^{\varepsilon,h}(x)(-D^0\phi_h^y)_j . $$ If $z=(x,v)$ and $z'=(y,w)$ are lifted phase-space states in $\mathbb R^{2d}$, the continuum and grid mean-field kernels are $$ \mathbb K_\varepsilon(z,z')=(v,cQ\,\mathcal E_\varepsilon(x,y)),\qquad \mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(z,z')=(v,cQ\,\mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h}(x,y)). $$
The spatial components are periodic in their position variables. A finite equal-weight system $\dot z_p=P^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^P\mathbb K_{\varepsilon,h}(z_p,z_r)$ uses particle charge $Q/P$ and mass $M/P$. No claim about the limit $\varepsilon\to0$ is part of this definition.

For fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and periodic grid, the smooth-branch weights $w_j^{\varepsilon,h}$ of [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]] are $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb T_L^d$. For every multi-index $\beta$, $\max_j\|\partial^\beta w_j^{\varepsilon,h}\|_\infty<\infty$. They are nonnegative and sum to one at every point.

For any real grid array $s$, define its mean-zero periodic Poisson pseudoinverse by
$$ A_h^\dagger s:=\text{the unique mean-zero grid array }u\text{ such that }A_hu=s-\bar s\,\mathbf1, $$
where $\bar s=L^{-d}\langle s,\mathbf1\rangle_h$. This definition is well-defined by [[thm-periodic-centered-difference-poisson-zero-mode-and-gauge]]. It gives $A_hA_h^\dagger s=s-\bar s\mathbf1$, $A_h^\dagger\mathbf1=0$, and a linear self-adjoint map on the full finite grid space.

derivations.claim: By [F2], each grid weight is smooth and has bounded derivatives of every finite order. By [F1], $\mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h}$ is a finite sum of products of such weights and fixed matrix entries, so it is $C^\infty$ and all its derivatives are bounded. In particular, both derivative suprema $M_x^{\varepsilon,h},M_y^{\varepsilon,h}$ are finite. More explicitly, if $B_{jk}$ are the vector entries of $-D^0A_h^\dagger$ and $C_w=\max_j\|\nabla w_j\|_\infty$, then $M_x^{\varepsilon,h}\le |cQ|h^{-d}C_w \sum_{j,k}|B_{jk}|\|w_k\|_\infty,\qquad M_y^{\varepsilon,h}\le |cQ|h^{-d}C_w \sum_{j,k}|B_{jk}|\|w_j\|_\infty ,$ which are finite explicit bounds for the defining suprema.

Any finite-order derivative of the continuum series multiplies each coefficient by finitely many components of $\kappa_k$. The coefficient already has one factor $|\kappa_k|^{-1}$; after $r$ additional derivatives, its magnitude is bounded by a constant times $(1+|k|)^r\prod_a\alpha_\varepsilon^{2|k_a|}$. These bounds are summable because each one-dimensional geometric series with a polynomial factor converges. Thus every differentiated series converges uniformly, and all derivatives are bounded. In particular, for a first derivative the factor $|\kappa_k|$ cancels the denominator $|\kappa_k|^2$, so its norm is bounded by the displayed sum times $|cQ|/L^d$. Periodicity permits the same bounds on Euclidean lifts.

First change $z=(x,v)$ while holding $z'=(y,w)$ fixed. The output difference has components $(v-\widetilde v,cQ(\mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h}(x,y)-\mathcal E_{\varepsilon,h}(\widetilde x,y)))$. Its squared Euclidean norm is at most $|v-\widetilde v|^2+(M_x^{\varepsilon,h})^2|x-\widetilde x|^2$, hence its norm is at most $\max\{1,M_x^{\varepsilon,h}\}|z-\widetilde z|$. Next change $z'$ while holding $\widetilde z$ fixed; this changes only the field component, by at most $M_y^{\varepsilon,h}|z'-\widetilde z'|$. Adding these bounds gives the stated two-variable estimate with $L_{\varepsilon,h}$. The same block-norm calculation using the continuum derivative bounds from step 1.2 gives the estimate with $L_\varepsilon$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $d\ge1$, let $U:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be continuously differentiable, and let $M$ be a real symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix. Write $\nabla U$ for its Euclidean gradient, and let $\epsilon>0$.

For $a,b\in\mathbb R$, define the **force kick** and **drift shear**
$$K_a(q,p)=(q,p-a\nabla U(q)),\qquad D_b(q,p)=(q+bM^{-1}p,p).$$
The one-step leapfrog map is
$$\Phi_\epsilon=K_{\epsilon/2}\circ D_\epsilon\circ K_{\epsilon/2},$$
where composition is read right to left. For a finite integer $L\ge1$, its $L$-step map is $\Phi_\epsilon^L$. Define the momentum flip $R(q,p)=(q,-p)$ and the flipped proposal map $T_{\epsilon,L}=R\circ\Phi_\epsilon^L$.

Each kick and drift is a continuous bijection with inverse $K_{-a}$ or $D_{-b}$, respectively. These finite maps use only $\nabla U$ and do not require a solution of Hamilton's ODE. The classical derivative of a force kick is not part of this definition: for merely $U\in C^1$, $\nabla U$ need not be differentiable.

Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, $V\in C^2(Q)$, and $M$ be symmetric positive definite. Put $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-I&0\end{pmatrix}$. At every point of their open domains, the local kick and drift from [[def-local-leapfrog-domain-on-an-open-configuration-set]] are $C^1$ and their Jacobians $A$ satisfy $A^TJA=J$. Here this matrix identity is the finite-regularity meaning of symplecticity; no smooth-manifold definition is being applied to a map of insufficient regularity.

Under the hypotheses of [[lem-canonical-kick-and-drift-shears-have-symplectic-jacobians]], every admitted local leapfrog step and every admitted kick-then-drift symplectic Euler step is a $C^1$ map with continuous Jacobian satisfying $D\Phi^TJD\Phi=J$ on its open admitted domain. The result concerns symplecticity, not energy conservation.

Let $d\ge1$, $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, $V\in C^3(Q)$, and $M$ symmetric positive definite. Set $H(q,p)=\tfrac12p^TM^{-1}p+V(q)$ and $F(q,p)=(M^{-1}p,-\nabla V(q))$. Fix $T>0$ and $h=T/N$ with $N\ge1$. Suppose the exact solution, numerical states, all kick/drift intermediate states, and every line segment used below lie in one compact convex tube $K\Subset Q\times\mathbb R^d$, with the derivatives of $F$ through order two bounded there. For $z_0$ in that tube, write $e_n^E$ for the error of iterated kick-then-drift symplectic Euler and $e_n^V$ for the error of iterated local leapfrog relative to the exact solution at $t_n=nh$. Write $\Psi_h^E$ and $\Psi_h^V$ for their admitted one-step maps and $\varphi_h$ for the exact flow. For sufficiently small $h$, constants $C_E,C_V,L$ independent of $h,N,n$ satisfy
$$\|\Psi_h^E(z)-\varphi_h(z)\|\le C_Eh^2,\qquad \|\Psi_h^V(z)-\varphi_h(z)\|\le C_Vh^3$$
for admitted $z\in K$, and whenever $nh\le T$,
$$e_n^E\le e^{LT}e_0+C_ETe^{LT}h,\qquad e_n^V\le e^{LT}e_0+C_VTe^{LT}h^2.$$
Thus symplectic Euler has global order one and leapfrog has global order two on the stated controlled tube. No unconditional domain-admissibility claim is made.

$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

For the Hamiltonian grid model of [[def-periodic-pic-separable-hamiltonian-grid-model]], let $\phi=A_h^\daggerho(X)$. Its position gradient is
$$ 
abla_{X_p}U_h(X)=q_p\sum_{j\in J_N}
abla w_j^{\varepsilon,h}(X_p)\phi_j . $$
Along every differentiable solution of $\dot X=M^{-1}p$, $\dot p=-

Reversing the composition gives $\Phi_{\Delta t}^{-1}=K_{-\Delta t/2}\circ D_{-\Delta t}\circ K_{-\Delta t/2}=\Phi_{-\Delta t}$. All maps are global on the periodic lift, so no intermediate-domain restriction is lost.

The potential is smooth, hence $C^2$, and $M$ is symmetric positive definite. Each admitted kick and drift satisfies the symplectic Jacobian identity [F2]; composing the three maps preserves that identity by the chain rule, as stated in [F3].

The Jacobian of a kick is $\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\-\frac{\Delta t}{2}\nabla^2U_h&I\end{pmatrix}$ and the Jacobian of a drift is $\begin{pmatrix}I&\Delta t M^{-1}\\0&I\end{pmatrix}$. Each is block triangular with identity diagonal blocks, so its determinant is $1$; multiplicativity gives $\det D\Phi_{\Delta t}=1$. The global kick/drift maps are $C^1$ diffeomorphisms, so [A1] permits applying [F5] to the map and its inverse, proving preservation of Lebesgue volume.

Let $\eta_\varepsilon$ be the explicit product kernel in [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]], with $\alpha_\varepsilon=e^{-\varepsilon/L}\in(0,1)$. Let $\mu$ be a finite signed Borel measure on $\mathbb T_L^d$ with mass $Q$ and total variation $\|\mu\|_{\rm TV}$. Put
$$ \widehat\mu(k)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}e^{-2\pi i k\cdot y/L}\,d\mu(y),\qquad \kappa_k=2\pi k/L . $$ Then $\eta_\varepsilon$ is strictly positive, even, smooth, and has integral one. The regularized neutralized source $$ \rho_\varepsilon^\mu(x)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}\eta_\varepsilon(x-y)\,d\mu(y)-Q/L^d $$ is $C^\infty$ with zero mean. Its unique zero-mean periodic solution of $-\Delta\phi_\varepsilon^\mu=\rho_\varepsilon^\mu$ is the absolutely and uniformly differentiable Fourier series $$ \phi_\varepsilon^\mu(x)=L^{-d}\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}} \frac{\left(\prod_{a=1}^d\alpha_\varepsilon^{|k_a|}\right)\widehat\mu(k)} {|\kappa_k|^2}e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}. $$
For every integer $r\ge0$, all spatial derivative series of order at most $r$ converge absolutely and uniformly; their bounds may depend on $r,\varepsilon,L,\|\mu\|_{\rm TV}$.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and a finite signed Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb T_L^d$ with total mass $Q$. Let $\rho_\varepsilon=\eta_\varepsilon*\mu-Q/L^d$ and let $\phi_\varepsilon$ be its unique zero-mean periodic Poisson potential from [[thm-periodic-pic-continuum-regularized-poisson-kernel-is-smooth]]. Put $E_\varepsilon=-\nabla\phi_\varepsilon$. Use the shape and periodic centered-difference Poisson operator of [[def-periodic-pic-shape-assignment-and-gather]] and [[def-periodic-pic-grid-and-inner-product]]. Let $s_h=P_h^\varepsilon\mu-Q/L^d$, let $A_h\phi_h=s_h$ with $\bar\phi_h=0$, set $E_{h,j}=-D^0\phi_h$, and gather $G_hE_h$ using the same shape. Define
$$ C_{\rm dep}=\frac{C_\eta\|\eta_\varepsilon\|_\infty}{Z_{\min}}\|\mu\|_{\rm TV},\quad C_{\rm FD}=\frac1{12}\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_a^4\phi_\varepsilon\|_\infty,\quad C_{\rm src}=C_{\rm dep}+C_{\rm FD}, $$ where $C_\eta,Z_{\min}$ are from [[lem-periodic-pic-shape-partition-and-quadrature-bound]]. Put $$ C_3=\frac16\left(\sum_{a=1}^d\|\partial_a^3\phi_\varepsilon\|_\infty^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad C_{\rm int}=\frac{C_{\eta,E}+\|E_\varepsilon\|_\infty C_\eta}{Z_{\min}}, \quad C_{\eta,E}=\frac{L^d}{12}\sum_{a=1}^d \sup_{x,y\in\mathbb T_L^d}\left|\partial_{y_a y_a}[\eta_\varepsilon(y-x)E_\varepsilon(y)]\right|_2 . $$ For vector fields, $\|V\|_\infty=\sup_x|V(x)|_2$ (the maximum of Euclidean lengths for grid fields); the derivatives in $C_{\eta,E}$ use this same Euclidean norm. Then the source $s_h$ is compatible and $$ \|G_hE_h-\eta_\varepsilon*E_\varepsilon\|_\infty \le L^{d/2}h^{2-d/2}\left(\gamma_{N,L}C_{\rm src}+C_3\right) +C_{\rm int}h^2. $$
The displayed $\gamma_{N,L}$ is the actual finite-grid inverse/derivative norm of [[thm-periodic-pic-poisson-residual-to-gathered-force-bound]] and satisfies $\gamma_{N,L}\le L/4$. Thus for $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ this fixed-$\varepsilon$ force error tends to zero as $h\to0$. Every constant depends on the stated smooth regularized solution and kernel; this is not an $\varepsilon\to0$ estimate.

Let $d\ge1$, let $U:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be continuously differentiable, and let $M$ be a real symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix. Write $\nabla U$ for its Euclidean gradient, and let $\epsilon>0$.

For $a,b\in\mathbb R$, define the **force kick** and **drift shear**
$$K_a(q,p)=(q,p-a\nabla U(q)),\qquad D_b(q,p)=(q+bM^{-1}p,p).$$
The one-step leapfrog map is
$$\Phi_\epsilon=K_{\epsilon/2}\circ D_\epsilon\circ K_{\epsilon/2},$$
where composition is read right to left. For a finite integer $L\ge1$, its $L$-step map is $\Phi_\epsilon^L$. Define the momentum flip $R(q,p)=(q,-p)$ and the flipped proposal map $T_{\epsilon,L}=R\circ\Phi_\epsilon^L$.

Each kick and drift is a continuous bijection with inverse $K_{-a}$ or $D_{-b}$, respectively. These finite maps use only $\nabla U$ and do not require a solution of Hamilton's ODE. The classical derivative of a force kick is not part of this definition: for merely $U\in C^1$, $\nabla U$ need not be differentiable.

For the Hamiltonian grid model of [[def-periodic-pic-separable-hamiltonian-grid-model]], let $\phi=A_h^\daggerho(X)$. Its position gradient is
$$ 
abla_{X_p}U_h(X)=q_p\sum_{j\in J_N}
abla w_j^{\varepsilon,h}(X_p)\phi_j . $$
Along every differentiable solution of $\dot X=M^{-1}p$, $\dot p=-
abla_XU_h(X)$, the continuous semidiscrete energy $H_h(X(t),p(t))$ is constant. This is an invariant of the exact finite-grid ODE; no time-discrete energy conservation is asserted.

Let $H_h(X,p)=\frac12p^TM^{-1}p+U_h(X)$ be [[def-periodic-pic-separable-hamiltonian-grid-model]], with $M$ symmetric positive definite and $U_h\in C^3(\mathbb R^{dP})$ periodic. Let $\Phi_{\Delta t}=K_{\Delta t/2}\circ D_{\Delta t}\circ K_{\Delta t/2}$ be the leapfrog map with the kick and drift conventions of [[def-leapfrog-step-map]]. Then:

1. For every signed step $\Delta t$, $\Phi_{\Delta t}^{-1}=\Phi_{-\Delta t}$.
2. Every step is symplectic.
3. Assuming Countable Choice, every step preserves Lebesgue volume on phase space.
4. On a finite interval $[0,T]$, if the exact and numerical paths, all kick/drift stages, and all line segments in the comparison lie in a common compact convex tube and the Hamiltonian vector field has bounded derivatives through order two there, the leapfrog trajectory error is at most $C_VTe^{LT}\Delta t^2$ for exact initialization and sufficiently small $\Delta t=T/n$.

The exact continuous flow conserves $H_h$ by [[thm-periodic-pic-hamiltonian-force-is-a-gradient-and-conserves-energy]]. No claim says the leapfrog map preserves $H_h$ exactly or that modified-energy estimates hold outside the analytic tube hypotheses of the geometric-integration suppliers.

derivations.claim: The half kick gives $p_{1/2}=p_0-(\Delta t/2)q_0=-1/4$. The drift gives $q_1=q_0+\Delta t p_{1/2}=1-(1/2)(1/4)=7/8$. The final half kick gives $p_1=p_{1/2}-(\Delta t/2)q_1=-1/4-7/32=-15/32$.

For the oscillator, $\dot q=p$ and $\dot p=-q$, so $\frac{d}{dt}H=qp-pq=0$. The kick and drift matrices for the test are $K_{1/4}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1/4&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad D_{1/2}=\begin{pmatrix}1&1/2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.$ Each has determinant one. Direct multiplication gives $A^TJA=(\det A)J=J$ for every real $2\times2$ matrix $A$, where $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$, so their composition is symplectic. The shears have inverses $K_{-1/4}$ and $D_{-1/2}$; reversing the palindromic composition with these inverses proves the step reversible. The exact Hamiltonian at the updated point is $H(q_1,p_1)=\frac12\left(\frac{49}{64}+\frac{225}{1024}\right)=\frac12\frac{1009}{1024}=\frac{1009}{2048},$ while $H(q_0,p_0)=1/2=1024/2048$. Their difference is $-15/2048$. Therefore this reversible symplectic step does not preserve its Hamiltonian exactly. The separate PIC results [F2] and [F3] concern their own variational force and tube hypotheses and are not transferred to this scalar test.
